label: ass:V-sym
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:V-sym}
The value matrix $ {F_V}\in \mathbb{R}^{d\times d } $ is nonsingular and symmetric, of eigenvalues $ \lambda_1>  \lambda_2 \geq \ldots \geq \lambda_d $ with $ \lambda_1 >0 $ simple and positive.
head: environment

label: lem:moja-equil1
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
An equilibrium point $ \bm{x}_i $ satisfies $ \bm{x}_i^+ = \bm{x}_i$ for all $i$, hence, from \eqref{eq:update-moja2}, $ \bm{x}_i = \frac{\tilde{\bm{x}}_i}{\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \|}  $, which implies that $ \tilde{\bm{x}}_i$ and $ \bm{x}_i $ must be collinear, i.e., $ \tilde{\bm{x}}_i = \varphi  \bm{x}_i $ for some $ \varphi \in \mathbb{R}$.
If $ \bm{y} =   \frac{1}{n}{F_V} \sum_{j=1}^n  \bm{x}_j$, then from \eqref{eq:update-moja2}, $ \tilde{\bm{x}}_i = \bm{x}_i + \eta \bm{y}  $ holds iff also $\bm{y}  $ and $ \bm{x}_i $ are collinear or $ \bm{y} =0$.
This condition can be written equivalently using projections as 
 \[
\Pi_{\bm{x}_i} \bm{y} =  (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T )\bm{y}   =0 .
 \]
 There are 3 cases in which this  can happen:
\begin{enumerate}
\item consensus: $ \bm{y} = \varphi_i \bm{x}_i $, for some scalar $ \varphi_i >0$;
\item bipartite consensus: $ \bm{y} = -\varphi_i \bm{x}_i $, for some scalar $\varphi_i >0$;
\item polygonal equilibria: $ \bm{y} =0$.
\end{enumerate}
In fact, in the first two cases, $ \Pi_{\bm{x}_i} \bm{x}_i = \pm  \varphi_i (\bm{x}_i - \bm{x}_i  \bm{x}_i^T \bm{x}_i ) = 0$, since $ \bm{x}_i^T \bm{x}_i =1$. The third case follows trivially.
To show that consensus must be an eigenvector of ${F_V}$, observe that at this equilibrium point we have  $ \bm{y}= {F_V} \bm{x}_i $, since $ \bm{x}_i= \bm{x}_j $.
Combining with $ \bm{y}= \varphi_i \bm{x}_i $, we have $  {F_V} \bm{x}_i =\varphi_i \bm{x}_i $, i.e., $ \bm{x}_i $ is an eigenvector of ${F_V}$ and $ \varphi_i$ one of its eigenvalues. The argument for bipartite consensus is identical. 

\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md:
For a given $ \bm{v}_k$ there are $ 2^n $ possible consensus or bipartite consensus equilibria.
These are always paired by a global symmetry w.r.t. the origin, i.e., if $ \bm{x}_i = \bm{v}_k $ $ \forall\, i$  is a consensus equilibrium point, its antipodal point $ \bm{x}_i = - \bm{v}_k $ $ \forall\, i$ is also a consensus equilibrium point, and similarly for the bipartite consensus equilibria.
This is implicitly assumed from now on, but  not explicitly written, to avoid overloading the formulation of the results.
head: environment

label: thm:moja-DT
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:moja-DT}
For the system \eqref{eq:update-moja}, under Assumption~\ref{ass:V-sym}, if 
$ \eta< \min \left( \frac{2}{ |\lambda_1 + \lambda_d |}, \, \frac{1}{2 \max \{  \lambda_1 , | \lambda_d | \} }  \right) $, 
the principal consensus equilibrium $ \bm{x}_i=\bm{v}_1 $ $\forall \, i$ is asymptotically stable, while all other consensus equilibria, all bipartite consensus equilibria (including those aligned with $ \bm{v}_1$), and all polygonal equilibria are unstable.
The trajectories of all tokens $ \bm{x}_i(t)$ converge to $ \bm{v}_1 $ (or to $ - \bm{v}_1 $) for almost all initial conditions $ \bm{x}_i(0)$.

label: lem:Jac-moja
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
head: manual

label: lem:moja-F-eigenvalues
title: Lemma
head: environment

label: eq:JacobF-moja
title: Proof
body_md:
When computing the Jacobian \eqref{eq:Jacob-moja} at the consensus $ \bm{x}_i=\bm{v}_k $ $\forall \, i$, we get
\begin{equation}
 \begin{split}
 J(\bm{v}_k) & = \left.  \frac{\partial f(\bm{x})}{\partial \bm{x}}  \right|_{\bm{x}_i = \bm{v}_k} \\
 & = \mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T \otimes \left(  \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k) \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} - \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_k \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k }  \right) \\
 & \;\;  + I \otimes \left(   \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k)  I - \eta \lambda_k (1-\eta \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \right).
 \end{split}
 \label{eq:JacobF-moja}
 \end{equation}
 where we have used $ \bm{v}_k^T ( I - \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T) =0$.
 The first term represents a factor present in all entries of $J(\bm{v}_k) $, while the second one is present only on the diagonal.
 For $ J(\bm{v}_k) $ there are 3 classes of eigenvectors:
 \begin{enumerate}
 \item The eigenvectors of the first class depend on the sign of $ 1+ \eta \lambda_k $. If $ 1+ \eta \lambda_k >0$, then choose $ \bm{p} = [ 0 \ldots 0 \; \bm{v}_k \; 0 \ldots 0 ] $ and compute the two components of $ J(\bm{v}_k) $:
 \[
 \begin{cases}
&  \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k) \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} - \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_k \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k 
= \frac{\frac{\eta}{n} (1 -1)}{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k  =0 \\ 
& 
 \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k)  I - \eta \lambda_k (1-\eta \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k =
  \frac{ 1 - \eta \lambda_k ( 1- \eta \lambda_k ) }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k
  \end{cases}
\]
meaning that 
\[
J(\bm{v}_k ) \bm{p} = \frac{ 1 - \eta \lambda_k  + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{p}
\]
i.e., $ \frac{ 1 - \eta \lambda_k  + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k }  $ is an eigenvalue of $ J(\bm{v}_k)$ of multiplicity $ n$ (as there are $n$ possible slots for $ \bm{v}_k $ in $ \bm{p}$).
If instead $ 1+ \eta \lambda_k <0 $, then choose the following $ n$ eigenvectors
\[
\bm{p} = \begin{cases} \bm{p}_1 =  [\bm{v}_k \; \bm{v}_k \ldots \bm{v}_k ]  \\
 \bm{p}_\ell = [\phi_1^\ell \bm{v}_k \;  \phi_2^\ell \bm{v}_k \ldots \phi_n^\ell \bm{v}_k ] \; \text{s.t.} \; \sum_i \phi_i^\ell =0 , \\
 \qquad \qquad \qquad  \qquad \qquad \qquad  \;\; \ell=2, \ldots, n
 \end{cases}
 \]
 In correspondence of $ \bm{p}_1 $, one gets 
 \[
 \begin{cases}
&  \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k) \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} - \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_k \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k 
=\frac{\eta}{n}  \frac{ - 2 \lambda_k }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k   \\ 
& 
 \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k)  I - \eta \lambda_k (1-\eta \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k =
  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2 }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_k
  \end{cases}
\]
hence 
\[
\begin{split}
J(\bm{v}_k) \bm{p}_1 & = \eta  \frac{ - 2 \lambda_k }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{p}_1 +  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{p}_1 \\
& = \frac{-1-3 \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2 }{1+ \eta \lambda_k }  \bm{p}_1 
\end{split}
\]
while in correspondence of $ \bm{p}_\ell $ one gets
\[
\begin{split}
J(\bm{v}_k) \bm{p}_\ell & = \begin{bmatrix} \sum_i \phi_i^\ell \left( \frac{\eta}{n}   \frac{ - 2 \lambda_k }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \right) \bm{v}_k +  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \phi_1 \bm{v}_k \\
\vdots \\
\sum_i \phi_i^\ell \left( \frac{\eta}{n}   \frac{ - 2 \lambda_k }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \right) \bm{v}_k +  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \phi_n \bm{v}_k
\end{bmatrix} \\
& =  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } \bm{p}_\ell 
\end{split}
\]
i.e., $  \frac{ -1 - \eta \lambda_k + \eta^2 \lambda_k^2  }{1+ \eta \lambda_k } $ is an eigenvalue of multiplicity $ n-1$. 

\item For the second class of eigenvectors choosing $ \bm{q}_h = [ \bm{v}_h\, \ldots \, \bm{v}_h] $ for $ h\neq k$, leads to 
\[
 \begin{cases}
&  \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k) \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} - \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_k \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_h 
=\frac{\eta}{n}  \frac{  \lambda_h }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{v}_h  \\ 
& 
 \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k)  I - \eta \lambda_k (1-\eta \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{v}_h =
  \frac{ 1  }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{v}_h
  \end{cases}
\]
and hence to 
\[
J(\bm{v}_k) \bm{q}_h = \frac{1 + \eta \lambda_h }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{q}_h 
\]
i.e., $ \frac{1 + \eta \lambda_h }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} $ is an eigenvalue of $ J(\bm{v}_k)$. There are $ d-1 $ such eigenvalues. 
\item The remaining $ nd-d-n+1 $ eigenvectors are assembled by considering vectors $ \bm{r} =\begin{bmatrix} (\bm{z}^1)^T & (\bm{z}^2)^T & \ldots  & (\bm{z}^n)^T \end{bmatrix}^T$ s.t. $ \bm{v}_k^T \bm{z}^i =0 $ for all $ i =1, \ldots, n $ and all $ h=1, \ldots, k-1, k+1, \ldots, d $ and $ \bm{q}_h^T \bm{r} =0 $. Since the number of such constraints is $ d-1+n$, there exist $ nd- n-d+1 $ such vectors $ \bm{r}$, and they can always be chosen so that  $ \sum_{i=1}^n  \bm{z}^i =0 $.
Computing,
\[
 \begin{cases}
&  \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k) \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} - \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_k \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{z}^i 
= \frac{\eta}{n} \frac{ {F_V} }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{z}^i  \\ 
& 
 \frac{{\rm sgn}(1+ \eta \lambda_k)  I - \eta \lambda_k (1-\eta \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k \bm{v}_k^T }{1 + \eta \lambda_k } \bm{z}^i =
  \frac{ 1  }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{z}^i
  \end{cases}
\]
hence
\[
J(\bm{v}_k) \bm{r} =   \frac{ 1  }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \begin{bmatrix}  \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_i \bm{z}_i + \bm{z}_1 \\
\vdots \\
 \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_i \bm{z}_i + \bm{z}_n
\end{bmatrix} =   \frac{ 1  }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |} \bm{r}
\]
\end{enumerate}
\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip
head: manual

label: rem:two-classes
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:two-classes}
The discrete-time system \eqref{eq:update} can be seen as a map from the manifold $ (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $ to itself. 
Hence its tangent space is $ T_{\bm{x}}  (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $, of dimension $ n (d-1)$, while the Jacobian $ J(\bm{x})$ computed above is in dimension $ nd $. 
Such Jacobian is what is sometimes called the ``extrinsic Jacobian'' living in the ambient manifold $ \mathbb{R}^{ nd \times nd}$ rather than in $ T_{\bm{x}}  (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $. 
What decides stability is however the ``intrinsic Jacobian'' living on  $ T_{\bm{x}}  (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $. For Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-F-eigenvalues}, if we look at the eigenvectors, we can easily deduce that the first class of eigenvectors (of cardinality $n$) does not belong to $ T_{\bm{x}}  (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $, while the other two classes are always in $ T_{\bm{x}}  (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n $, hence it is only these last two classes that decide the stability character of the equilibria.
head: environment

label: lem:moja-consensus-stab
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the  principal consensus equilibrium point $ \bm{v}_1$ and the eigenvalues of $ J(\bm{v}_1)$ computed in Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-F-eigenvalues}. 
Notice from Remark~\ref{rem:two-classes} that only the second and third class of eigenvalues matter for the stability.
Under Assumption~\ref{ass:V-sym}, $ 1 + \eta \lambda_1 >1$, hence the 3rd class of eigenvalues is inside the unit disk. When $ | \lambda_d | < \lambda_1 $, then also the second class is inside the disk for all $ h=2, \ldots, d$, regardless of the sign of $ \lambda_h$, while when $ - \lambda_d >\lambda_1 $ we need to have $  \frac{1+ \eta \lambda_d }{ 1+ \eta \lambda_1 } >-1 $, i.e., $ \eta <  \frac{-2}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_d } = \frac{2}{| \lambda_1 + \lambda_d |} $. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
                                                                                                    
    
               
                                                                                                                                    
                                                                       
             
    
                                                        
       
                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                
       

When $ k>1$ (consensus at non-principal eigenvectors), then one of the eigenvalues of $ J(\bm{v}_k) $ is $ \frac{1 + \eta \lambda_1 }{|1+ \eta \lambda_k |}  $ which is always $ >1 $. This is obvious when $ \lambda_k \geq 0 $, as $ \lambda_k< \lambda_1$. What needs to be checked is the case of $ \lambda_k $ negative with $ - \lambda_k \gg \lambda_1 $. 

For this case we consider the two situations
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $ 1 + \eta \lambda_k >0 $, then we have $ \frac{1 + \eta \lambda_1 }{ 1+ \eta \lambda_k }>1$ because this is equivalent to $ 1 + \eta \lambda_1 > 1+ \eta \lambda_k $. 

\item If $ 1 + \eta \lambda_k <0 $, then we must show that it is $ - \frac{1 + \eta \lambda_1 }{ 1+ \eta \lambda_k }>1$, i.e., that $ 1 + \eta \lambda_1 > - 1 - \eta \lambda_k$, or $ \eta (\lambda_1 + \lambda_k) >-2$. As $ \lambda_1 + \lambda_k<0$, the expression holds if it holds for the largest possible value of $ \eta $.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
Taking $ \eta = \frac{2}{| \lambda_1 + \lambda_d|}$, we obtain the following inequality $ - \frac{2(\lambda_1 + \lambda_k)}{\lambda_1 + \lambda_d}>-2 $, or, equivalently, $ \lambda_1 + \lambda_k > \lambda_1 + \lambda_d$ which is always true. 
\end{enumerate}
In both situations $ J(\bm{v}_k) $ has an eigenvalue outside the unit disk. 
\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip
head: manual

label: lem:moja-bip-consensus-stab
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moja-bip-consensus-stab}
For the system \eqref{eq:update-moja}, under Assumption~\ref{ass:V-sym}, the bipartite consensus equilibria, $ \bm{x}_i=\pm \bm{v}_k $ $\forall \, i$ are all unstable $ \forall \, k =1, \ldots, d$ and $ \forall \, \eta>0$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At a bipartite consensus equilibrium there exists at least one index $ i \in \mathcal{V}_1 $. Consider the perturbation $ \bm{x}_i = \bm{v}_k + \bm{w}_i  $ with $ \bm{v}_k^T \bm{w}_i =0$ $ \forall \, i$. For this perturbation, the unnormalized next iterate is 
\[
\begin{split}
\tilde{\bm{x}}_i & = \bm{v}_k+\bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V}\sum_j (\bm{v}_k + \bm{w}_j) \\
& = ( 1+ \eta \nu \lambda_k ) \bm{v}_k + \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j 
\end{split}
\]
and its norm
\[
\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \| = \left( \alpha^2\left( 1+ \frac{\| \bm{u}_i \|^2 }{\alpha^2} \right) \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\]
where $ \alpha := 1 + \eta \nu \lambda_k $, $ \bm{u}_i := \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j $, and we have used $ \bm{v}_k^T \bm{v}_k =1 $ and $ \bm{v}_k^T \bm{w}_i =0 $.
Hence, using the binomial series expansion ($ (1 + \xi)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\approx 1 - \frac{\xi}{2}  + h.o.t. $), 
\[
\begin{split}
\bm{x}_i^+ &= \frac{\tilde{\bm{x}}_i}{\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \|}
= \frac{ \alpha \bm{v}_k + \bm{u}_i }{  \alpha \left( 1+ \frac{\| \bm{u}_i \|^2 }{\alpha^2} \right) ^{\frac{1}{2}} } 
\approx \bm{v}_k + \frac{\bm{u}_i}{\alpha} + h.o.t. \\
&= \bm{v}_k + \frac{ \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j }{ 1+ \eta \nu \lambda_k }  + h.o.t.\\
& \approx  \bm{v}_k + ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k ) ( \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j ) 
\end{split}
\]
where we have used the expansion $ \frac{1}{1+ \eta \nu \lambda_k } \approx 1-  \eta \nu \lambda_k$. 
The linearized equation is then 
\[
\bm{w}_i^+ =  ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k )  \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j .
\]
Expanding all $ \bm{w}_i $ in the orthonormal basis $ \bm{v}_1, \ldots, \bm{v}_d $, and denoting $ \bm{w}_i = \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell $, 
\[
\bm{w}_i^+ = \sum_\ell (\xi^i_\ell)^+ \bm{v}_\ell =  ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k ) \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell + \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_{j, \ell} \lambda_\ell \xi^j_\ell  \bm{v}_\ell .
\]
Projecting along $ \bm{v}_1 $, 
\[
(\xi^i_1)^+ =  ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k ) \xi^i_1 +\frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_1 \sum_j \xi^j_1 .
\]
If $ \bm{\xi}_1 := [ \xi_1^1 \ldots \xi_1^n ]^T$, then these $ n$ difference equations can be written in vector form as
\[
\bm{\xi}_1^+ =  ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k ) \bm{\xi}_1 + \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_1 \mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T \bm{\xi}_1 .
\]
We need to compute the eigenvalues of the $ n \times n$ matrix $ M(k,1) = ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k )I + \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_1 \mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T $. 
One such eigenvalues is associated to the consensus vector $ \mathds{1} \in \mathbb{R}^d$:
\[
 M(k,1) \mathds{1} = ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k ) \mathds{1} +  \eta  \lambda_1 \mathds{1} = ( 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k +\eta \lambda_1 ) \mathds{1} .
 \]
 If $ k\neq 1 $ then either $ \lambda_k >0 $ and $ \lambda_k < \lambda_1$, or $ \lambda_k<0$. Since $ \nu<1$, in both cases $ 1- \eta \nu \lambda_k +\eta \lambda_1 >1 $ and the bipartite equilibrium point is unstable. 
 If $ k=1$, then $ 1+\eta(1-\nu) \lambda_1 >1$, i.e., also in this case we have found an eigenvalue outside the unit disk, and hence the equilibrium point is unstable. 
\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip
head: manual

label: lem:moja-polygonal-stab
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:moja-polygonal-stab}
For the system \eqref{eq:update-moja}, under Assumption~\ref{ass:V-sym}, all polygonal equilibria are unstable.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At a polygonal equilibrium point $ \bm{x}=\bm{s} =[\bm{s}_1 \, \dots \, \bm{s}_n] $, consider the perturbation $ \bm{x}_i = \bm{s}_i + \bm{w}_i  $ with $ \bm{s}_i^T \bm{w}_i =0$ $ \forall \, i$. For this perturbation, the unnormalized next iterate is 
\[
\begin{split}
\tilde{\bm{x}}_i & = \bm{s}_i+\bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V}\sum_j (\bm{s}_j + \bm{w}_j) \\
& =\bm{s}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} \underbrace{{F_V}\sum_j \bm{s}_j}_{=0} + \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n}  {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j 
\end{split}
\]
and its norm
\[
\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \| = \left( 1+ \| \bm{u}_i \|^2 +2  \frac{\eta}{n}  \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j  \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\]
where $ \bm{u}_i := \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j $, and we have used $ \bm{s}_i^T \bm{w}_i =0 $.
Hence, using the binomial series expansion ($ (1 + \xi)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\approx 1 - \frac{\xi}{2}  + h.o.t. $), 
\[
\begin{split}
\bm{x}_i^+ &= \frac{\tilde{\bm{x}}_i}{\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \|}
= \frac{  \bm{s}_i + \bm{u}_i }{ \left( 1+ \| \bm{u}_i \|^2 + 2  \frac{\eta}{n}  \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j  \right) ^{\frac{1}{2}} } \\
&\approx (\bm{s}_i + \bm{u}_i) \left(1- \frac{\| \bm{u}_i \|^2}{2} -   \frac{\eta}{n}  \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j \right)  + h.o.t. \\
&= \bm{s}_i + \bm{u}_i -   \frac{\eta}{n}  \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j \bm{s}_i  + h.o.t.\\
& = \bm{s}_i + \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} (I - \bm{s}_i \bm{s}_i^T) {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j + h.o.t.
\end{split}
\]
The linearized equation is then 
\[
\bm{w}_i^+ = \bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} (I - \bm{s}_i \bm{s}_i^T) {F_V} \sum_j \bm{w}_j .
\]
Expanding all $ \bm{w}_i $ and $ \bm{s}_i $ in the orthonormal basis $ \bm{v}_1, \ldots, \bm{v}_d $, and denoting $ \bm{w}_i = \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell $ and $ \bm{s}_i = \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell $, 
\[
\begin{split}
\bm{w}_i^+ & = \sum_\ell (\xi^i_\ell)^+ \bm{v}_\ell \\
& =  \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell + \frac{\eta}{n} \left( I - \sum_h \zeta^i_h \bm{v}_h \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell^T \right)  \sum_{j, \ell} \lambda_\ell \xi^j_\ell  \bm{v}_\ell \\
& =  \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell + \frac{\eta}{n} \left( I - \sum_h \zeta^i_h \bm{v}_h \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell  \lambda_\ell \sum_j  \xi^j_\ell  \right).
\end{split}
\]
Recall that $ {F_V}$ has always at least one positive eigenvalue $\lambda_1 >0$. We can always choose $ \bm{w}$ s.t. each $ \bm{w}_j $ has a nonzero component in the direction of the associated eigenvector $ \bm{v}_1$: $ \xi^j_1\neq 0$.
Projecting along $ \bm{v}_1 $
\[
(\xi^i_1)^+ = \xi^i_1 + \frac{\eta}{n} \left( 1-{\zeta_1^i}  \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell  \lambda_\ell \sum_j  \xi^j_\ell \right).
\]
If the perturbation is such that $ \bm{w}_i $ has only a component along $ \bm{v}_1 $, $ \xi_1^i\neq 0$, $ \xi_j^i=0$ $ \forall \, j \neq i$, then
\[
(\xi^i_1)^+ = \xi^i_1 + \frac{\eta}{n} ( 1-{\zeta_1^i}^2) \lambda_1 \sum_j \xi^j_1 .
\]
If $ \bm{\xi}_1 :=  \begin{bmatrix} \xi_1^1 &\ldots &\xi_1^n\end{bmatrix}^T$ and $  \bm{\zeta}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} \zeta^1_1 & \ldots & \zeta^n_1 \end{bmatrix}^T$, then in vector form
\[
\begin{split}
\bm{\xi}_1^+ & =  \bm{\xi}_1 + \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_1 \left( I- Z_1^2 \right)\mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T \bm{\xi}_1 \\
& = \left( I+ \frac{\eta}{n} \lambda_1 \left( I- Z_1^2 \right)\mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T \right) \bm{\xi}_1 .
\end{split}
\]
where $ Z_1 = {\rm diag}(\bm{\zeta}_1)$. 
Since $ \bm{s} $ is not an eigenvector of ${F_V}$, it is $ |\zeta^i_1 |< 1$. From $ \lambda_1 >0$, it is then $\rho(I +\eta \lambda_1(I-Z_1^2) \mathds{1} \mathds{1}^T)>1 $, meaning that when $ \bm{\xi}_1 = \epsilon \mathds{1}$ for some scalar coefficient $ \epsilon$ the system diverges, hence the polygonal equilibrium point $ \bm{s}$ is unstable.

label: lem:layp-moja
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:layp-moja}
The function $ W(\bm{x}) = -\frac{1}{2 n^2} \left( \sum_{j=1}^n \bm{x}_j^T {F_V} \sum_{j=1}^n \bm{x}_j  \right)$ is a Lyapunov function for  \eqref{eq:update-moja}. When $  \eta\leq \frac{1}{2 \|{F_V}\|}  $ it guarantees that  \eqref{eq:update-moja} converges to one of the equilibria determined in Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-equil1}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since the state space is compact,  all functions arising in the expansion of the Lyapunov function $ W(\bm{x})  $ (and hence also of its increment) are uniformly bounded. For the second order truncation of the increment $ W(\bm{x}^+) - W(\bm{x}) $, it is possible to compute an explicit bound on $ \eta $ for which the increment is guaranteed to be nonincreasing.
From \eqref{eq:update-moja2},  using the binomial series expansion $ (1 + \xi)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\approx 1 - \frac{\xi}{2}  + \frac{3}{8} \xi^2 + O(\xi^3) $  
\[
\begin{split}
 & \bm{x}_i^+  = \frac{\tilde{\bm{x}}_i}{\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \| } \\
 & = (\bm{x}_i + \eta \bm{y} )  \left(1- \eta \bm{x}_i^T \bm{y}  + \frac{\eta^2}{2} \left( 3 (\bm{x}_i^T \bm{y} )^2 - \| \bm{y}\|^2   \right) + O(\eta^3)  \right) \\
 & = \bm{x}_i +\eta g_i + \eta^2 \left( \frac{3}{2} r_i^2 \bm{x}_i  - \frac{1}{2} \| \bm{y}\|^2 r_i - r_i \bm{y} \right) + O(\eta^3)  
 \end{split}
 \]
 where we have indicated $ r_i := \bm{x}_i^T \bm{y} $ and $ g_i= g(\bm{x}_i ) := (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) \bm{y} $.
 The increment of $ W$ up to second order in $ \eta $ is then 
 \[
 \begin{split}
 & W(\bm{x}^+) - W(\bm{x}) = \\
 & =  -\frac{1}{2 n^2} \left( \sum_{j=1}^n (\bm{x}_j^+)^T {F_V} \sum_{j=1}^n \bm{x}_j^+  - \sum_{j=1}^n \bm{x}_j^T {F_V} \sum_{j=1}^n \bm{x}_j  \right) \\
 = & - \frac{\eta^2}{2 n^2} \left( 2 n \bm{y}^T \sum_j \left( \frac{3}{2} r_i^2 \bm{x}_i - \frac{1}{2} \| \bm{y}\|^2 \bm{x}_i - r_i \bm{y} \right) \right. \\
 & \left. + \sum_j g_j^T {F_V} \sum_j g_j \right) - \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_j g_j^T \bm{y} + O(\eta^3) \\
 = &  - \frac{\eta^2}{ n} \left(  \sum_j  \left( \frac{3}{2} r_j^2 \bm{y}^T \bm{x}_j - \frac{1}{2} \| \bm{y}\|^2 \bm{y}^T \bm{x}_j - r_j \bm{y}^T \bm{y} \right) \right. \\
 & \left. + \frac{1}{2n}  \sum_j g_j^T {F_V} \sum_j g_j \right)  - \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 + O(\eta^3)  \\
 = & - \frac{\eta^2}{ n} \left( \frac{3}{2} \sum_j r_i  (r_i^2 - \| \bm{y} \|^2 ) + \frac{1}{2n}  \sum_j g_j^T {F_V} \sum_j g_j  \right) \\
 &  - \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 + O(\eta^3)  \\
  = & \;  \frac{\eta^2}{ n} \left( \frac{3}{2} \sum_j r_i  \| g_j \|^2 - \frac{1}{2n}  \sum_j g_j^T {F_V} \sum_j g_j  \right) \\
 &  - \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 + O(\eta^3)  \\
 \end{split}
 \]
 where we have used idempotency of the projection $ (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T)$ to get
 \[
 \begin{split}
 g_i^T \bm{y} & = \bm{y}^T (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) \bm{y} \\
 & = \bm{y}^T (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T)(I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) \bm{y} = \| g_i\|^ 2\\
 \|\bm{y}\|^2 - r_i^2 & = \bm{y}^T \bm{y} - \bm{y}^T \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T \bm{y} = \bm{y}^T (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) \bm{y} \\
 & = \bm{y}^T (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i^T) \bm{y} = g_i^T g_i = \| g_i \|^2 .
 \end{split}
 \]
 Since $ \| \sum_j g_j \|^2 \leq n \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 $, it is
 \[
 - n \| {F_V} \| \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 \leq \sum_j g_j^T {F_V} \sum_j g_j \leq n \| {F_V} \| \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 .
 \]
  Furthermore
 \[
 - \| {F_V} \| \leq - \| \bm{y} \| \leq r_i \leq  \| \bm{y} \| \leq \| {F_V} \| .
 \]
 These lead to the inequality
 \[
 \begin{split}
  W(\bm{x}^+)  & - W(\bm{x})   \leq  - \frac{\eta}{n} \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 \\
 & +\frac{\eta^2}{n} \left( \frac{3}{2} \| {F_V} \| \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 + \frac{1}{2} \| {F_V} \| \sum_j \| g_j \|^2 \right) 
 \end{split}
 \]
 or
 \[
 W(\bm{x}^+) - W(\bm{x}) \leq \frac{\eta}{n}  \left(  - 1 + 2 \eta \| {F_V} \| \right) \sum_j \| g_j \|^2.
 \]
 Hence when $ \eta\leq \frac{1}{2 \|{F_V}\|} $ we have $  W(\bm{x}^+) - W(\bm{x}) \leq 0$. 
 Since the sequence $ W(\bm{x} (k) ) $ (where $k$ is the time index) is nonincreasing and bounded below, it must converge. Moreover, summability of the increments implies $ \sum_{k=0}^\infty \sum_{i=1}^n \| g(\bm{x}_i(k)) \|^2 < \infty $, hence $  \| g(\bm{x}_i(k)) \| \to 0 $ for each $i$. 
 At an equilibrium point $ \bm{x} $ it must then be $ g(\bm{x}_i) = (I - \bm{x}_i \bm{x}_i) \bm{y} =0 $ for all $ i$, i.e., $ \bm{y} $ must be collinear with $ \bm{x}_i $. Recalling Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-equil1}, this implies that $ \bm{x} $ must be a consensus or a bipartite consensus equilibrium point. 
 \hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip

The proof of the theorem is simply the composition of the results of Lemmas~\ref{lem:moja-F-eigenvalues},~\ref{lem:moja-consensus-stab},~\ref{lem:moja-bip-consensus-stab},~\ref{lem:moja-polygonal-stab} and~\ref{lem:layp-moja}.

head: manual

title: Remark
body_md: Clustering equilibria own their name to the fact that typically multiple agents are found at the same value. In particular we say that $ \bm{x}_1, \ldots, \bm{x}_n$ are at an $ m$-clustering equilibrium point if $ \bm{x}_i \in \{ \bm{w}_1, \ldots, \bm{w}_m \}$ with $ 1 \leq m \leq n$, i.e., if $ \bm{x}_1, \ldots, \bm{x}_n$ cluster at the $m$ vectors $ \bm{w}_1, \ldots, \bm{w}_m$. Notice that some $ \bm{w}_i $ can be eigenvectors of ${F_V}$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: A clustering equilibrium can be a consensus, i.e, $ \bm{x}_i  = \bm{x}_j $ for all $ i,j$, but with $ \bm{x}_i $ which is not aligned with any eigenvector of ${F_V}$, i.e., $ \bm{x}_i \nparallel  \bm{v}_k $ $ \forall \, k$. We refer to these as 1-clustering, while the ``consensus'' characterization is reserved for the case $ \bm{x}_i \parallel \bm{v}_k $ for some $k$. A 2-clustering instead typically is s.t. $ \bm{x}_i \in \{ \bm{w}_1, \bm{w}_ 2\}$ $ \forall \, i$, with $ \bm{w}_1 \neq - \bm{w}_2 $.
head: environment

label: prop:clustering-eq
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:clustering-eq}
The system  \eqref{eq:update} has a clustering equilibrium $ \bm{x} \in (\mathbf{S}^{d-1})^n $ iff $ \exists $ scalars $ \theta_1, \ldots, \theta_n $ s.t. the matrix $I_n \otimes I_d  -(\Theta \otimes I_d) (A(\bm{x}) \otimes I_d)(I_n\otimes {F_V})$ is singular, where $ \Theta={\rm diag}(\theta_1, \ldots, \theta_n )$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In vector form, the clustering equilibrium condition $ \bm{x}_i =  \theta_i  {F_V} \sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}(\bm{x})  \bm{\bm{x}}_j $ becomes $ \bm{x} = (\Theta \otimes I_d) (A(\bm{x}) \otimes I_d)(I_n\otimes {F_V})  \bm{x}$, where $ \bm{x}^T = [ \bm{x}_1^T \, \ldots\, \bm{x}_n^T ]$. 
Rewriting it as $  (I_n \otimes I_d -(\Theta \otimes I_d) (A(\bm{x}) \otimes I_d)(I_n\otimes {F_V})) \bm{x} =0 $, the algebraic equation has nontrivial solutions if and only if the matrix $I_n \otimes I_d  -(\Theta \otimes I_d) (A(\bm{x}) \otimes I_d)(I_n\otimes {F_V})$ is singular.
\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip
head: manual

title: Remark
body_md: From the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:clustering-eq}, it is $ \bm{x} = (\Theta \otimes I_d) (A(\bm{x}) \otimes I_d)(I_n\otimes {F_V})  \bm{x}$, where $ \bm{x}^T = [ \bm{x}_1^T \, \ldots\, \bm{x}_n^T ]$. It follows that if $ \bm{x}_1, \ldots, \bm{x}_n$ form an $m$-clustering equilibrium point, then also the antipodal point  $ -\bm{x}_1, \ldots, -\bm{x}_n $ is an $ m$-clustering equilibrium point because $ A(\bm{x}) = A(-\bm{x})$. If in a clustering equilibrium only some (but not all) $ \bm{x}_i $ flip sign, then the new state is typically no longer an equilibrium point.

label: lem:cons-Aij
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At a consensus equilibrium $ \bm{x}_i = \bm{v}_k $ for all $ i $, and $ A_{ij}(\bm{x}) $ is composed of all equal terms
\[ 
A_{ij}(\bm{x}) = \frac{e^{  \bm{v}_k^T {F_Q}^T{F_K}\bm{v}_k  } }{\sum_{\ell=1}^n e^{\bm{v}_k^T {F_Q}^T{F_K} \bm{v}_k } }= \frac{1}{n}.
\]
At a bipartite consensus point $ \bm{x}_i = \pm \bm{v}_k $, split the $n$ tokens into two sets $ \mathcal{V}_1 $ and $ \mathcal{V}_2 $, $ \mathcal{V}_1\cup \mathcal{V}_2 = \{ 1, \ldots, n \}$,  according to whether $ \bm{x}_i =\bm{v}_k $ or $ \bm{x}_i =- \bm{v}_k$ at equilibrium. Assume that $ n_1 = | \mathcal{V}_1|  $ tokens are equal to $ \bm{v}_k $ and $ n_2 = | \mathcal{V}_2 | $ equal to $ -\bm{v}_k$, with $ n_1 + n_2 =n$. 


Four different entries appear in $ A_{ij}(\bm{x})$, two due to the denominator (depending on whether $ \bm{x}_i =\bm{v}_k $ or $ \bm{x}_i =- \bm{v}_k $), and two due to the numerator (depending on whether $ \bm{x}_i$ and $ \bm{x}_j $ have the same sign). 
    
                                                                                                                                    
   
More specifically, denoting  $ \alpha_1^k = e^{  \bm{v}_k^T {F_Q}^T{F_K} \bm{v}_k }  $ and $ \alpha_2^k = e^{ - \bm{v}_k^T {F_Q}^T{F_K} \bm{v}_k } $, then the entries of the attention matrix are 
\[ 
A_{ij}(\bm{x}) 
= \begin{cases} 
\frac{\alpha_1^k}{n_1 \alpha_1^k + n_2 \alpha_2^k} & \text{if}\; i \in \mathcal{V}_1, j \in \mathcal{V}_1 \\ 
\frac{\alpha_2^k}{n_1 \alpha_1^k + n_2 \alpha_2^k}  & \text{if}\; i \in \mathcal{V}_1, j \in \mathcal{V}_2 \\ 
\frac{\alpha_2^k}{n_1 \alpha_2^k + n_2 \alpha_1^k}   & \text{if}\; i \in \mathcal{V}_2, j \in \mathcal{V}_1 \\ 
\frac{\alpha_1^k}{n_1 \alpha_2^k + n_2 \alpha_1^k}   & \text{if}\; i \in \mathcal{V}_2, j \in \mathcal{V}_2  .
   \end{cases}
\]
Letting $ \beta_1^k = n_1 \alpha_1^k + n_2 \alpha_2^k$, and $ \beta_2^k = n_1 \alpha_2^k + n_2 \alpha_1^k$ and assuming w.l.o.g. that the first $ n_1 $ agents are in $ \mathcal{V}_1 $ and the last $ n_2 $ in $ \mathcal{V}_2 $, the attention matrix is 
\begin{equation}
A(\bm{x}) = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{\beta_1^k} ( \alpha_1^k & \ldots & \ldots & \alpha_1^k & \alpha_2^k & \ldots & \alpha_2^k) \\
\vdots & & & \vdots & \vdots & & \vdots \\
\frac{1}{\beta_1^k} ( \alpha_1^k & \ldots & \ldots & \alpha_1^k & \alpha_2^k & \ldots & \alpha_2^k) \\
\frac{1}{\beta_2^k} ( \alpha_2^k &  \ldots &  \ldots & \alpha_2^k & \alpha_1^k & \ldots &\alpha_1^k) \\
\vdots & & & \vdots  & \vdots & &  \vdots \\
\frac{1}{\beta_2^k} ( \alpha_2^k & \ldots &  \ldots & \alpha_2^k & \alpha_1^k & \ldots & \alpha_1^k) 
\end{bmatrix} ,
\label{eq:A-bipart}
\end{equation}
from which it is obvious that the rank must be 2. 

As for an $m$-clustering equilibrium point with vectors $ \bm{w}_1, \ldots, \bm{w}_m$, following a similar procedure it is easy to realize that since $ \bm{w}_i \neq \bm{w}_j $ and $ {F_Q}^T {F_K}$ is not symmetric,  there are $ m^2 $ different entries in the numerators of $A_{ij}$, and only $m$ in the denominators. Rearranging the entries as in \eqref{eq:A-bipart}, each row of $A$ has exactly $m$ different terms, and a block counting argument leads to $ {\rm rank}(A)=m$.

label: lem:Jacob-self
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The partial derivatives of $ A_{ij}(\bm{x}) $ are 
 \[
 \begin{split}
  \frac{\partial A_{ij} (\bm{x}) }{\partial \bm{x}_h}  
  = &  \frac{\partial }{\partial \bm{x}_h}  \frac{e^{\langle {F_Q} \bm{x}_i, {F_K} \bm{x}_j \rangle } }{\sum_{\ell=1}^n e^{\langle {F_Q} \bm{x}_i, {F_K} \bm{x}_\ell \rangle } }\\
 =  & -  \bm{x}_i^T {F_Q}^T {F_K} A_{ij} (\bm{x}) A_{ih}(\bm{x}) \\
 & +  \bm{x}_i^T {F_Q}^T {F_K} A_{ij} (\bm{x})\delta_{jh} \\
&  + \bm{x}_j^T {F_K}^T {F_Q} A_{ij} (\bm{x})\delta_{ih}  \\
& - \sum_\ell \bm{x}_\ell^T {F_K}^T {F_Q} A_{i\ell} (\bm{x})A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \delta_{ih} 
 \end{split}
 \]
 or \eqref{eq:partial-A} after regrouping.
Similarly to the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:Jac-moja},  the series expansion of the normed term is
\[
\begin{split}
& \chi( \bm{x}) =  \left(  (  \bm{x}_i +  \eta \bm{y}_i )^T (  \bm{x}_i + \eta \bm{y}_i) \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}  
                                                                                     
\\
& \approx  1 + \frac{1}{2} \left( 2  \eta \bm{x}_i ^T \bm{y}_i + \eta^2 \| \bm{y}_i \|^2  \right) - \frac{1}{2}  \eta^2 ( \bm{x}_i^T \bm{y}_i ) ^2 + O(\eta^3) \\
& =  1 + \eta \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j + \frac{\eta^2}{2} \left( \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j^T {F_V}^T {F_V} \cdot \right. \\
& \left. \cdot \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j - ( \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j)^2 \right)  + O(\eta^3)
\end{split}
\]
Differentiating it
\[
\begin{split}
&  \frac{\partial \chi(\bm{x})}{\partial \bm{x}_h }  =   \,  \eta \,  \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \left(  \sum_j \bm{x}_j  \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{x})}{\partial \bm{x}_h}  + A_{ih}(\bm{x}) I \right) \\
&   + \eta^2 \left(  \sum_j \bm{x}_j^T A_{ij}(\bm{x}) {F_V}^T {F_V}  \left(  \sum_j \bm{x}_j \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{x})}{\partial \bm{x}_h}   + A_{ih}(\bm{x})I \right) 
 \right. \\
&  \left. -  \left( \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j \right) \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \right. \cdot \\
& \cdot \left.  \left(  \sum_j\bm{x}_j  \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{x})}{\partial \bm{x}_h}   + A_{ih}(\bm{x}) I\right) \right) + \left( \eta  \sum_j \bm{x}_j^T A_{ij}(\bm{x}) {F_V}^T \right. \\
& \left. - \eta^2  \left( \bm{x}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{x}) \bm{x}_j \right)\sum_j \bm{x}_j^T A_{ij}(\bm{x}) {F_V}^T \right) \delta_{ih}
\end{split}
\]
or \eqref{eq:Jac-attent1} after regrouping.
One gets the result inserting these quantities into \eqref{eq:jacon-atten1}.

title: Proof
body_md:
Notice first that, since $ |\gamma_i^k |\leq 1 $, $  | \lambda_k| \geq | \lambda_k \gamma_i^k | $, hence $\min\left( \frac{1}{\lambda_1 } , \, \frac{1}{ | \lambda_d |} \right)  \leq \frac{1}{ | \lambda_k| } \leq \frac{1}{ | \lambda_k \gamma_i^k |}$. 
Consequently, $ \eta< \min\left( \frac{1}{\lambda_1 } , \, \frac{1}{ | \lambda_d |} \right) $ implies $ \eta |  \lambda_k \gamma_i^k | \leq 1 $, or $ 1- \eta |  \lambda_k \gamma_i^k | >0$, which in turn implies $ 1 + \eta \lambda_k \gamma_i^k \geq 0 $, $ i=1,2$.

label: lem:polyg-self
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:polyg-self}
The polygonal equilibria are all unstable for \eqref{eq:update}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The idea of the proof is similar to that used in Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-polygonal-stab} for the multiagent Oja flow. 
A polygonal equilibrium point $ \bm{x} =\bm{s} =\begin{bmatrix} \bm{s}_1 & \ldots & \bm{s}_n \end{bmatrix} \in (\mathbb{S}^{d-1})^n$ is s.t. $ {F_V}  \sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{s}_j  =0$. Let us compute the linearization of \eqref{eq:update} at $\bm{s}$, obtained perturbing $ \bm{s}$ with a perturbation $ \bm{w} = [ \bm{w}_1 \ldots \bm{w}_n] $ with  $  \bm{s}_i^T \bm{w}_i =0$.  For the non-normalized next iterate it is
\[
\begin{split}
\tilde{\bm{x}}_i = & \bm{s}_i+\bm{w}_i + \frac{\eta}{n} {F_V}\sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{s} + \bm{w}) (\bm{s}_j + \bm{w}_j)  \\
= & \bm{s}_i + \eta \underbrace{{F_V}\sum_j A(\bm{s}) \bm{s}_j}_{=0} + \bm{w}_i + \eta  {F_V} \sum_j A(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \\
& +  \eta  {F_V} \sum_j \sum_h  \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{s})}{\partial \bm{w}_h}  \bm{w}_h \bm{s}_j + h.o.t.
\end{split}
\]
where the vectors $  \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{s})}{\partial \bm{w}_h}  $ are computed in \eqref{eq:partial-A}.
Denote $ \psi^{ij} (\bm{w}) := \sum_h \frac{\partial A_{ij}(\bm{s})}{\partial \bm{w}_h}   \bm{w}_h$ and observe that $ \psi^{ij} (\bm{w}) $ is a sum of bilinear forms $ \bm{s}_\ell B_k \bm{w}_h $ for some matrices $ B_k $ (see \eqref{eq:partial-A} for their specific expressions). 
Since $ \| \bm{s}_\ell \|=1$ and $  \bm{w}_h $ is small enough, from the matrix Cauchy-Schwartz inequality, for each of these bilinear forms it holds $ - \| B_k\|_2 \leq \bm{s}_\ell B_k \bm{w}_h \leq \| B_k \|_2 $, where $ \|B_k \|_2 $ is  independent of $ \bm{w}_h$. 


Denoting $ \bm{u}_i := \bm{w}_i + \eta {F_V}  \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right) $, the norm of $ \tilde{\bm{x}}_i $ is
\[
\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \| = \Big( 1+ \| \bm{u}_i \|^2 + 2 \eta \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right)  \Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}
\]
where we have used $ \bm{s}_i^T \bm{w}_i =0 $.
Observe that $ \| \bm{u}_i \|^2 $ is composed entirely of terms of order 2 or higher in $ \bm{w}_i $, hence, using the binomial series expansion ($ (1 + \xi)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\approx 1 - \frac{\xi}{2}  + h.o.t. $), 
\[
\begin{split}
& \bm{x}_i^+ = \frac{\tilde{\bm{x}}_i}{\| \tilde{\bm{x}}_i \|}
\approx (\bm{s}_i + \bm{u}_i) \left(1- \frac{\| \bm{u}_i \|^2}{2} \right. \\
&\qquad  \left. - \eta \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right) \right)  + h.o.t. \\
&\approx  \bm{s}_i - \eta \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right) \bm{s}_i  + \bm{u}_i   + h.o.t.\\
& = \bm{s}_i - \eta  \bm{s}_i  \bm{s}_i^T {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right)+ \bm{w}_i\\
& \qquad  + \eta {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right) + h.o.t.\\
& = \bm{s}_i + \bm{w}_i +\eta (I - \bm{s}_i  \bm{s}_i^T ) {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right).
\end{split}
\]
The linearized equation is then 
\[
\bm{w}_i^+ = \bm{w}_i +\eta (I - \bm{s}_i  \bm{s}_i^T ) {F_V} \sum_j \left( \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \bm{s}_j + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \bm{w}_j \right).
\]
Expanding all $ \bm{w}_i $ and $ \bm{s}_i $ in the basis of eigenvectors $ \bm{v}_1, \ldots, \bm{v}_d $, and denoting $ \bm{w}_i = \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell $ and $ \bm{s}_i = \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell $, 
\[
\begin{split}
\bm{w}_i^+ & = \sum_\ell (\xi^i_\ell)^+ \bm{v}_\ell =  \sum_\ell \xi^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell +\eta \Big( I - \sum_k \zeta^i_k \bm{v}_k \sum_\ell \zeta^i_\ell \bm{v}_\ell^T \Big) \cdot \\
& \quad   \cdot \sum_{j, \ell} \lambda_\ell (\psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \zeta^j_\ell + A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \xi^j_\ell )  \bm{v}_\ell .
\end{split}
\]

Assuming that the perturbation $ \bm{w}$ is aligned with $ \bm{v}_1$, i.e., for all $i$, $ \xi^i_1 \neq 0 $ and $ \xi^i_k=0$ for $ k=2, \ldots, d$, then, projecting along $ \bm{v}_1$, yields
\[
{\xi^i_1}^+ =\xi^i_1 + \eta \left( 1- (\zeta^i_1)^2 \right) \lambda_1 \Big( \sum_j \psi_{ij}(\bm{w}) \zeta^j_1 +  \sum_j A_{ij}(\bm{s}) \xi^j_1 \Big) .
\]
Denoting  $ \bm{\xi}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} \xi^1_1 & \ldots & \xi^n_1 \end{bmatrix}^T$
and $  \bm{\zeta}_1 = \begin{bmatrix} \zeta^1_1 & \ldots & \zeta^n_1 \end{bmatrix}^T$ the collection of the $ \xi_1^i $ and $ \zeta_1^i $ components of all agents, the previous ODEs can be expressed in vector form as
\begin{equation}
{\bm{\xi}_1}^+ =\bm{\xi}_1 + \eta  \lambda_1 \left( I- Z_1^2 \right) \left( \Psi \bm{\zeta}_1 + A(\bm{s} ) \bm{\xi}_1 \right)
\label{eq:ode-eta-self}
\end{equation}
where $ Z_1 = {\rm diag}(\bm{\zeta}_1)$, $ \Psi =[\psi_{ij}]$ is a matrix with lower and upper bounds independent of $ \bm{w}$, and $ \bm{\zeta}_1 $ is fixed. $ A(\bm{s} ) $ is a row stochastic matrix,  $ \rho(A(\bm{s} )) =1 $ and $ A(\bm{s} ) \mathds{1} = \mathds{1}$. 
Since $ |\zeta^i_1 |< 1$ because  $ \bm{s} $ is not an eigenvector of ${F_V}$ and $ \lambda_1 >0$, it is $\rho(I +\eta \lambda_1(I-Z_1^2) A(\bm{s}))>1 $, and the system \eqref{eq:ode-eta-self} diverges when $ \bm{\xi}_1 = \epsilon \mathds{1}$ for some scalar $ \epsilon$. Hence the polygonal equilibrium $ \bm{s}$ is unstable. 
\hfill \vrule height 5pt width 5pt depth 0pt \medskip

body_md:
Under the assumption of the theorem, the system~\eqref{eq:update-multihead-auton-bis} has the consensus points at the eigenvectors of $F$ as equilibria, as can be verified by an argument similar to Lemma~\ref{lem:self-equil1}. In particular, when $ \bm{x}_i$ approaches a consensus point, the attention matrices of \eqref{eq:update-multihead-auton-bis} still approach a uniform matrix: $ A_{ij}^{(h)}(\bm{x}) \to \frac{1}{n}$, $ h=1, \ldots, H$. Therefore we can use the same argument used in Theorem~\ref{thm:stab-main-self}: at consensus, the system \eqref{eq:update-multihead-auton-bis} has the Jacobian $ J(\bm{v}_k) $ of the multiagent Oja system \eqref{eq:update-moja}, whose eigenvalues were computed in Lemma~\ref{lem:moja-F-eigenvalues}. Consensus aligned with the principal eigenvector $ \bm{v}_1 $ is locally asymptotically stable, while all other consensus points at the other eigenvectors of $F$ are unstable.
